{{Short description|Condition in probability theory for stochastic processes}}
In [[probability theory]], '''Novikov's condition''' is the sufficient condition for a [[stochastic process]] which takes the form of the [[Radon–Nikodym derivative]] in [[Girsanov's theorem]] to be a [[martingale (probability theory)|martingale]]. If satisfied together with other conditions, Girsanov's theorem may be applied to a [[Brownian motion]] stochastic process to change from the original [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] to the new measure defined by the Radon–Nikodym derivative.

This condition was suggested and proved by [[Alexander Novikov (mathematician)|Alexander Novikov]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Novikov |first=A. A. |date=1972 |title=On an identity for stochastic integrals |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1117088 |journal=Theory of Probability and its Applications |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=717-720 |doi=10.1137/1117088|url-access=subscription }}</ref> There are other results which may be used to show that the Radon–Nikodym derivative is a martingale, such as the more general criterion [[Kazamaki's condition]], however Novikov's condition is the most well-known result.

Assume that
<math> (X_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}</math> is a real valued adapted process on the probability space <math> \left (\Omega, (\mathcal{F}_t), \mathbb{P}\right) </math> and <math>(W_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}</math> is an adapted [[Brownian motion]]:<ref name=Pasc>{{cite book |last=Pascucci |first=Andrea |year=2011 |title=PDE and Martingale Methods in Option Pricing |location=Milan |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] |series=Bocconi & Springer |volume=2 |isbn=978-88-470-1780-1 }}</ref>{{rp|334}}

If the condition

: <math>   
\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac12\int_0^T|X|_t^2\,dt}   \right]<\infty
</math>

is fulfilled then the process

: <math>
  \ \mathcal{E}\left( \int_0^t X_s \; dW_s \right) \ = e^{\int_0^t X_s\, dW_s  -\frac{1}{2}\int_0^t X_s^2\, ds},\quad 0\leq t\leq T
</math>

is a martingale under the probability measure <math>\mathbb{P}</math> and the [[filtration (mathematics)|filtration]] <math>\mathcal{F}</math>. Here <math>\mathcal{E}</math> denotes the [[Doléans-Dade exponential]].
